requirements.text: create a new HR case under the Beneficiaries topic, assign it to Diana Johnson in the 'HR Service Desk' group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 24 AND coe_type = 'Total Rewards' AND opened_for = 14 AND assignment_group = 4 AND assigned_to = 15 AND priority = 'moderate' AND status = 'draft' AND source = 'email'
requirements.source: Verify if the new case is created properly.
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id is 60)
the Beneficiaries topic (topic_detail 4) has two services; adding a nominee is an add or modify request, so hr_service 24 'Beneficiaries Add/Modify', not 25, which is an inquiry
coe_type Total Rewards: the Beneficiaries topic sits in the Benefits category, whose coe_type is Total Rewards
opened_for 14 is Kenneth Scott's HR profile (user 14); the column references hr_profile
assignment_group 4 is 'HR Service Desk'; assigned_to 15 is Diana Johnson, an active member of group 4, as the policy's assignment constraint requires
priority not stated; the policy's default for a new case is moderate
status draft: the policy sets every new case to draft
source email: the request came in by email from Kenneth Scott

requirements.text: he recently got married ... take care of updating his records accordingly
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_profile WHERE user_id = 14 AND marital_status = 'Married'
requirements.source: Verify if the user profile is updated.
assumptions: Kenneth Scott is user 14, with exactly one HR profile (14); its marital_status is Divorced on the seed
the record his marriage changes is marital_status, spelt Married as in the other profiles (Divorced, Married, Single)

disagreement: row: one pass anchors on hr_profile_id 14, the other selects user_id = 14; chose user_id = 14 because both name the same single row on the seed (profile 14 belongs to user 14) and the benchmark's check selects by user_id

Verify if the new case is created proper.evidence: opened_for, assignment_group and assigned_to are integer id columns (referencing hr_profile, user_group and user) and every seed case stores ids there; the check compares them with the names 'Kenneth Scott', 'HR Service Desk' and 'Diana Johnson', which no id equals, so they are replaced by hr_profile 14, group 4 and user 15; every other cell is kept

notes:
disagreement: value: the profile requirement's row: one pass anchors on hr_profile_id 14, the other selects user_id = 14; chose user_id = 14, since both name the same single row and the benchmark's check selects by user_id (resolved on that requirement).
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, cell and value and on both dispositions; their texts, assumptions and notes differ in wording only.
No table holds insurance beneficiaries or nominees, so adding the wife as nominee has no cell to test beyond the Beneficiaries case and the marital status.
The case's short_description template ('Service: , Subject: , Detail: .') and its 30 to 120 character limit come only from the policy's format rules, which the benchmark does not test, so they are left out.
opened_by is not fixed: Kenneth Scott made the request by email but the acting user, Scott Mitchell, registers the case, and the policy says the requester is typically the employee, a manager or an HR Specialist, so it is left untested.
The new case's org_id is not fixed: Kenneth Scott's profile is in org 6 while the service and the group are in org 1, so it is left untested.
The acting user, Scott Mitchell (user 41), holds the admin role, and the policy says an administrator must not perform routine HR case work; the request and the benchmark both expect the case created and the profile updated, so the requirements follow the request and the conflict is recorded here.
The policy's priority list (critical, high, medium, low) disagrees with its own default of moderate; the seed uses moderate, so moderate is kept.
